doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sorting out the chronology of the 1932-33 band and Doc Cheatham
summary: Berger and Carter work out that the Empire Ballroom was 1933, that the rehearsal band came earlier, and when Carter took up the trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I don’t remember at all. In Boston. Jesus, I don’t remember that.
But you recall an Empire Ballroom engagement around this time.
Yes, I think so.
That’s with your own band.
Yes.
I think the chronology that Morroe had done shows you opening the Empire Ballroom in February of ’33.
Yeah, I said thirty . . . oh, 33’, oh.
So that’s a little later. All of this that we’re talking about, this Boston thing . . .
Then the Empire Ballroom was ’33.
Right.
So that’s when I was trying to fool around with the trumpet, and Doc Cheatham gave me the mouthpiece.
Yes.
Yes, then it was ’33. See, I . . .
Well, I think this rehearsal band . . . so we’ll call it the rehearsal band for the . . .
Was earlier.
Was ’32.
Yeah, but Doc wasn’t in that, Doc Cheatham.
Okay, so by the time you started playing the trumpet was even later, maybe even 1933, which you . . .
Yeah, it was later.
And you, several months later, were already recording on it.
Oh, really? What did I record on it?
When you did Once Upon a Time.
Oh, that’s right. That was 1933.
So your development on trumpet was even in a shorter period than we originally thought.
I’m messed up with the time, really.
Well, Doc Cheatham was not in this band, at least in August or September of ’32, so . . .
No.
But he could have been in and out; it’s also possible, you know.
I don’t think so. I think the first time he worked for me after McKinney’s Cotton Pickers was at the Empire Ballroom.
Well, we can fortunately still ask him. [laughs]
That’s right. I hope he remembers. He’s done a lot of things, too, you know.
Yeah, one or two since then. [laughs]
That’s right.
